Before validators are defined as class methods
Wrap validators are the most flexible of all
Wrap validators allow you to run code before or after Pydantic and other validators process the input data
Wrap validators can terminate validation immediately by returning data early or raising an error
Both field and model validators can optionally take an extra `ValidationInfo` argument
`ValidationInfo` provides already validated data
`ValidationInfo` provides user-defined context
`ValidationInfo` provides the current validation mode ('python', 'json', or 'strings')
`ValidationInfo` provides the current field name for field validators
A model validator defined in a base class will be called during validation of a subclass instance
Overriding a model validator in a subclass will override the base class' validator

cases.query: TypeAdapter

claims.claim: TypeAdapter is a Pydantic class that lets you create an object with methods for validating, serializing, and producing JSON schemas for arbitrary types
TypeAdapter serves as a replacement for deprecated utility functions like `parse_obj_as` and `schema_of`
TypeAdapter covers some use cases of 'root' models
You can create a TypeAdapter for any type and use it to validate and serialize data
TypeAdapter should be instantiated once and reused rather than creating a new instance each time it's needed
Each instantiation of TypeAdapter constructs new validators and serializers
TypeAdapter supports configuration through a `config` argument using `ConfigDict`
Configuration cannot be provided if the type adapter directly wraps types that have their own config (BaseModel, TypedDict, or dataclass)
As of v2.10, TypeAdapter supports deferred schema building through the `defer_build` configuration option
Deferred schema building is helpful for types with forward references or expensive core schema builds
You can manually rebuild the schema using the `rebuild()` method
You may need to explicitly specify generic parameters for proper typing in some scenarios

cases.query: GZipMiddleware

claims.claim: GZipMiddleware is a middleware that handles GZip compression of responses for any request that includes "gzip" in the Accept-Encoding header
It supports both standard and streaming responses
In FastAPI, GZipMiddleware is imported from fastapi.middleware.gzip
minimum_size argument - Do not GZip responses smaller than this size in bytes. Defaults to 500
compresslevel argument - Integer from 1 to 9. Defaults to 9. Lower values result in faster compression but larger files; higher values result in slower compression but smaller files
thread_minimum_size argument - Compress body chunks at least this large in a worker thread. Defaults to 131072 (128 KiB)
exclude_content_types argument - Content types that are never compressed. Defaults to text/event-stream and already-compressed formats
The middleware will not GZip responses that already have a Content-Encoding set
The middleware will not GZip partial content responses (status 206)
The middleware will not GZip responses with excluded Content-Type values
